This is an unofficial fan system for the 1975 Empire of the Petal Throne rules, with an optional Swords & Glory background generator.

Attacks: target a token and click a weapon. The system reads the defender's armour class and magical armour, finds the score needed on Table I (men) or Table II (creatures), adds the attacker's talent and weapon bonuses, and offers a damage button on a hit. A natural 20 doubles the damage dice and offers the instant-death roll.

Damage: the number of dice comes from the damage dice table by attacker level against defender hit dice. Priests read one row up, Magic Users with a dagger two rows up; two- and three-dice beings start on rows II and III. Talent damage bonuses and weapon pluses are added once; missiles get no talent damage bonus.

Spells: each casting rolls d100 against the spell-working chance (level plus psychic bonus) and uses one daily casting. Use Dawn: regain spells each game morning.

Experience: Award Experience adds treasure and kills, applies the talent bonus and the reduced share at higher levels, and sets the level. Level Up rolls hit points, talent increase, original skill and bonus spell.

Once a week. Retribution: 1d6 per level. First-level characters cannot ask.

Any character may serve one God or one Cohort; Priests have special access, but every profession can receive advice and help. A character serving a good deity is aligned with good, one serving an evil deity with evil. Choose the deity on the character sheet; it lists the deities of the character's alignment (all of them for a neutral nonhuman).

Joining or changing: only at the beginning of an adventure. Go to the deity's temple, get a favourable reaction from its priests (Nonplayer Character Reaction Table, Sec. 1020), and pay an offering: the score of percentile dice multiplied by the score of a d10, "the latter representing thousands of Káitars" (as printed). The priests may also ask for a week or a month of study in the temple.

Names: the five good Gods are the Tlomitlányal and the five evil Gods the Tlokiriqáluyal ("-yal" is the Tsolyáni plural). Each God has a Cohort; the ten Cohorts are the Hlimékluyal. The 1975 rules call the two sides good and evil; later Tékumel books call them Stability and Change.

Divine intervention (Sec. 2110; tables on the Saving throws, morale and divine aid page): once a week at most, player characters only, never at Level I. Gods are harder to reach than Cohorts and should do proportionately more. Phrase requests clearly: the referee may exploit ambiguity ("Get us out of here!" may land the party in another city, continent or world).

Where the 1975 text is silent or ambiguous, this system makes the following choices. Each one is labeled in the sheet or item and can be changed.

Talent checks: the 1975 rules have no check against a single talent. Clicking a talent on the sheet rolls d100 and succeeds under the talent's score, the same method as the Sec. 725 Physical Action check; shift-click adds a modifier set by the referee.

Constitution 41-60 revival chance: not stated; 50% (between the 40% and 60% bands) is used.

Failed spells: the text does not say whether a failed roll uses up the day's casting. A world setting controls this (default: it does).

Creature saving throws: the save table covers professions only. Creatures save as a Warrior of level equal to their hit dice by default.

Hit dice values such as 6/10/16: small, medium and large specimens; the medium value is used for combat tables.

Hit dice beyond the table: the row for (level - 10) is added to the top row, matching both worked examples in Sec. 710.

Cure Serious Wounds: described among the priestly skills but missing from the order table; placed 9th following the descriptions.

Energy Bolt: the effect of a failed save is not stated.

Sling and bolas damage, thrown and sling range bands: not given separately; see each item.

Creature spellcasting: EPT gives creature casters a level (e.g. Ssú: Magic User of level IV-XV) but no Psychic Ability; their spell chance uses the Caster level field (hit dice when 0) with average Psychic Ability.

Magic user arms and armour: any dagger, steel or Chlén-hide; leather armour allowed (Sec. 721 over Sec. 920); a shield is flagged (AC 7 limit), helmets are not. Priests: slings and bolas count as non-edged; bows, crossbows and javelins are edged.

Species modifiers: S&G Sec. 2.223 changes to Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, Psychic Ability and Comeliness are added to nonhuman characters' EPT talents. Swamp Folk Psychic Ability is fixed at 1 (Non-Psychic). Ssú use the Grey Ssú values.

N'lüss modifiers: S&G Sec. 2.222 attribute changes (Strength +10, Dexterity -10, Intelligence -10, Psychic Ability -5) are added to the EPT talent scores while a Human's homeland is N'lüss.

Weapon length groups: weapons the S&G length list does not name were given a group by reading: EPT battleaxe, flail, morning star and mace 7; EPT spear 3; S&G one-handed mace row 8, longer mace or axe row 7; short spear or quarterstaff row 3 (5 for a quarterstaff). Change any weapon's group on its sheet.

Natural 20 with several damage dice: the number of damage dice is doubled and bonuses added once, per Sec. 731.

Initiative: a world setting chooses EPT reaction time (one d6 per side, sides by token disposition: Friendly = party, Hostile = foes, Neutral = others; ties roll again), Swords & Glory (d20 for every combatant, rerolled each round; optional weapon length order in round 1), or a d6 for each combatant.

Token sizes: stated length or width / 10 ft, rounded up (middle of a range); height does not count; no stated size = 1x1. Sized creatures take the footprint of the size rolled. The Aqáa's 20-60 ft is spread over its three sizes. Table choices where the book gives no measurement: Akhó 1x1 / 2x2 / 3x3 and Dlaqó 1x1 / 2x2 / 3x3 by size; Teqéqmu 1x1 / 2x2 / 2x2 by size; Tsi'íl ("huge") 2x2; Dzór (10-12 ft tall giants) 2x2.

Treasure numbers: EPT says to roll a d6 for the number of items. '1-3' is read as half a d6 rounded up; '2-12', '4-24' and '6-36' as 2, 4 or 6 d6; '1-100' as d100; '10-40' and '10-60' as d4 or d6 × 10.

Which amulet or miscellaneous magical item: EPT gives no die. A d12 is used for the twelve amulets and a d24 for the 24 items (as for books).

Gems: each gem is valued separately (EPT allows valuing groups of 5 or 10 when there are many). Jewelry already in the top row stays there.

Weapon spells (Sec. 1820.4): the table is read as 'a d100 score at or above the number gives that many spells', so stronger weapons have more spells.

Weapon powers (Sec. 1810): rolled for magic swords, scimitars and battle-axes, the weapons Sec. 1820 names.

NPC 'Sword and Dagger': the dagger is one of the three dagger results of the miscellaneous weapon table, picked at random. A Priest who gets a sword or edged weapon rolls again; spears, bows and arrows count as edged, as on the weapon items.

The Treatise of Hrsh: its d12 results overlap as printed (9-12, then 11 and 12); the text is kept as printed.
